title: Catalog paths, endpoint walkthrough, and copy lab notes
body:
Context and goal:

This is a lightweight lab doc capturing ideas and small wireframe notes for three related flows: model catalog discovery, a compact endpoint creation wizard, and the version pinning affordances we present to users. Purpose is to capture copy variants, edge cases, and groom a short backlog of UI tasks we should break into tickets. Keep this intentionally informal.

High-level constraints:
- Console must be compact for first-time users (<= 3 clicks from model selection to sample query).
- All copy should surface risk/cost consequences of pinning (cost, latency, rollback complexity) without being scary.
- Encourage safe defaults: suggest a pinned-but-auto-fallback variant for most teams.

1) Catalog discovery heuristics (wireframe notes)
- Left rail: filters (task: chat | text-gen | embeddings | rerank) + size (small/medium/large) + quantization (fp16/int8) + region.
- Primary list: card grid. Each card shows: model name, short descriptor (1 line), latency estimate (p95 @ small batch), cost band (low/medium/high), stars (community rating), pin icon state (unpinned / pinned to endpoint).
- Sorting defaults: relevance (search term match) -> latency-sensitive -> cost when user has cost-aware toggle ON.
- Search quirks: fuzzy matching + alias table (e.g., "vicuna" -> Vicuna v1.3 remapped). Keep a tooltip: "We normalize popular model names for easier search."

Microcopy candidates for empty-state and quick-help:
- Empty catalog search: "No models found. Try removing filters or searching for fewer terms."
- Tooltip for latency estimate: "Estimated p95 at 8-token output on a dedicated small GPU. Actual latency depends on request size and current load."
- Pin indicator hover: "This model is pinned by 2 endpoints. Click to view where it's used."

2) Endpoint quick-wizard (compact mode)
Wireframe sketch (3 steps in top progress bar): 1) select model, 2) inputs & routes, 3) review & create. Inline expanded options accessible via "Advanced" link.

Step details and copy drafts:
- Step 1 header: "Choose a model for this endpoint"
  - subcopy candidate A: "Pick a model to serve. You can pin a version now or let the platform pick the fastest compatible variant."
  - subcopy candidate B: "We recommend pinning for repeatable results — or choose adaptive routing to prioritize lower latency when available."
- Model card CTA: primary button "Use this model" secondary link "Preview"

Step 2: Inputs & routes
- Small form fields: route name (default: "/v1/generate"), token limit, temperature (slider), concurrency cap (recommended default based on plan).
- Microcopy for concurrency: "Concurrency sets how many simultaneous requests this endpoint will accept. Lower values reduce contention but can increase queueing."
- Error inline copy: "Concurrency must be an integer between 1 and 100."

Step 3: Review & create
- Top summary: model (name + pinned version if any), route, region, expected cost estimate for 1M tokens (low/med/high).
- Create button variants: "Create endpoint" (primary) and "Create endpoint, pin version" (danger-styled awareness? maybe primary + subtle badge).
- Confirmation toast: "Endpoint created — routing will start within ~15s. You can change the pinned version from the endpoint details."

Accessibility/keyboard notes:
- Wizard should trap focus in modals; ESC closes with a confirmation if there are unsaved changes.
- Sliders should have numeric input for keyboard users.

3) Version pinning semantics + copy treatments
Problems to solve in wording: users confuse "pin" with "freeze". They expect pin = route-level lock to an exact model binary, but we also want an option for pinned-to-major (soft pin). Proposed mental model: two modes — Exact Pin (hard) and Compatibility Pin (soft).

Copy framing options to test in copy lab:
- Exact pin label: "Pin exact model version"
  - tooltip: "Locks endpoint to a specific model build (including weights). Use when you need identical outputs over time. No automatic upgrades."
- Compatibility pin label: "Pin by compatibility"
  - tooltip: "Allow the platform to upgrade to compatible model builds that preserve API/behavior. Lower maintenance, but outputs may vary."

Fallback UX drafts:
- If a pinned exact model is unavailable in a region, show an endpoint banner: "Serving is temporarily degraded. We will route traffic to a compatible model in <region> unless you change pin settings."
- Banner CTAs: "Switch to compatibility pin" (primary) and "Pause endpoint" (secondary).

Copy for warnings about cost/latency:
- Soft nudge variant: "Pinning to older, larger models may increase latency and cost. We’ll show predicted impact before you confirm."
- Strong nudge variant: "Heads up — this version is unoptimized on GPUs in your selected region and may double serving costs."

4) Edge cases & grooming backlog (tickets)
- INF-TKT-01: Catalog: show "deprecated" badge for model versions that are EOL. Accept criteria: badge visible, tooltip with deprecation date + replacement suggestions.
- INF-TKT-02: Endpoint Wizard: validation for path uniqueness per project. AC: user cannot create two endpoints with identical route unless explicit confirmation.
- INF-TKT-03: Pinning: add an audit log entry and easy rollback action. AC: endpoint history shows who changed pin, timestamp, and quick-rollback button.
- INF-TKT-04: Region mismatch handling: If a pinned version is not available in the chosen region, surface a clear blocking error or offer a compatibility fallback. Decision needed: block vs fallback.
- INF-TKT-05: Copy A/B: run a small experiment on pinning microcopy (soft nudge vs strong nudge) measuring pin adoption rate and downstream rollback events.

Prioritization proposal (for grooming):
- P0: INF-TKT-02 (validation for duplicate paths) — obvious bug/risk.
- P1: INF-TKT-03 (pin audit + rollback) and INF-TKT-04 (region mismatch behavior) — operationally important.
- P2: INF-TKT-01 (deprecated badges) and INF-TKT-05 (copy experiment) — lower immediate risk.

Notes on observability integration:
- Endpoint summary should surface: last deploy time, pinned version id, p95 latency, token cost per 1k. Each should link to the console trace view.
- Consider a small "what changed" diff when changing pins — show model diff summary (e.g., weights size, tokenizer changes, known behavior deltas).

Sample text snippets to copy/paste into UI (final candidates):
- Model card tagline: "Small, fast LLM — great for chat and short completions."
- Endpoint review header: "Ready to create: 1 model • 1 route"
- Pin tooltip (final candidate): "Pin locks an endpoint to a model build. Choose exact pin for repeatability, or compatibility pin for safe automatic upgrades."
- Create success toast: "Endpoint live — try a test request from the console or use the SDK."

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Default pin behavior on create: should we default to compatibility pin or leave unpinned? (ops leaning: default to compatibility pin for safety + reproducibility).
- How prominently should cost impact be surfaced? (Provide simple low/med/high and allow detailed breakdown in an expandable row.)
- Block vs fallback for region-mismatched pins (see INF-TKT-04).

Next steps for this doc:
- Split the backlog items into ticket cards with ACs (I will create INF-TKT-02..04 in JIRA).
- Run a 1-week copy lab with product writers: test two pinning microcopy variants and collect qualitative notes from solutions engineers.
- Hand a small prototype to frontend for accessibility review (keyboard trapping + sliders).

Rough sketch links / references:
- Quick prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/endpoint-quick-wizard (placeholder)
- Related drive notes: shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/model-variant-selection-microcopy-and-ux-hypotheses.json

Notes to self / scratch lines:
- Try framing pin as "repro vs adapt" rather than "hard vs soft" — might be more intuitive.
- Keep CTA verbs concrete: "Create endpoint" beats "Done".

End.
